region.text: the Kingdom of Cochin as a Portuguese protectorate

ledger.note: 1505: 'the kingdom became a protectorate in 1505' (the fort of 1503 stood on allied Cochin territory).

region.text: Fort Manuel and the Portuguese enclave at Cochin

ledger.note: 15 August 1505: the State of India is established with its seat at Cochin. Infobox 'Established 15 August 1505'; Almeida took up residence at Cochin in 1505 and strengthened Fort Manuel (a fort had been built in 1503 on allied Cochin land); capital Cochin 1505-1530.

region.text: Goa: the island of Tiswadi with Old Goa, taken from Bijapur

ledger.note: 1510: Goa. 'Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate in 1510, and Velha Goa became the permanent settlement.' Malacca (1511) and Ormuz (1515) are also added to the State on the page but have their own dossiers.
1519: 'Quilon/Kollam (1519): became a Portuguese settlement'. The page does not name the ruler who yielded it.
1520: Rachol. 'Portugal extended its rule over the town after Krishnadevaraya delivered Rachol Fort.'
1530: the capital moves from Cochin to Velha Goa (Old Goa), the seat until 1843 (the viceroys lived in Panjim from 1 December 1759).

region.text: Salsette, the Bombay islands, Chaul and Bassein, the Northern Province given by the Sultan of Gujarat

ledger.note: 1534: the Northern Province. Salsette, the Bombay islands, Chaul and Bassein 'acquired from the Sultan of Gujarat' (Bombay known as Bom Bahia from 1535).
1535: Diu 'acquired in 1535 from the Sultan of Gujarat'.
1539: Daman. 'Sacked in 1531 and ceded in 1539' (the page does not name the ceding party; it sits under the Gujarat acquisitions).

1558: 'a Portuguese garrison was established on Male' (the Portuguese had arrived in the Maldives in 1507). An outpost of the Estado da India run from Goa; the mirror of the occupation recorded in maldives.
1573: 'a popular revolt led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu al-Auzam drove the Portuguese away.'

region.text: Bombay island (Bom Bahia), ceded to Charles II in 1661

ledger.note: 1661: Bombay goes to England. 'Ceded to Charles II of England in 1661 as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry.'

8 December 1661: the Dutch take Quilon ('An expedition, under Admiral Van Goens arrived in Quilon, capturing the city on the 8th of December 1661'); the page adds that the Portuguese had lost it earlier, in 1658-59.

region.text: the Kingdom of Cochin as a Portuguese protectorate

ledger.note: 1662-63: Cochin's Portuguese-backed Rani Gangadhara Lakshmi was captured on 5 February 1662 and handed to the Zamorin; afterwards 'the Kingdom of Cochin became a Dutch ally'. The page does not use the word protectorate.

region.text: Fort Manuel and the Portuguese enclave at Cochin

ledger.note: 6 or 7 January 1663: the garrison capitulates ('The forts of Cochin, Cannore and Quilon were to be handed over to the Dutch'); Cannanore fell on 15 February 1663 and Cranganore in 1662. Cannanore and Cranganore are not drawn: the Portuguese India page does not mention them.

region.text: most of the Northern Province including Bassein and Chaul (and Salsette, which the Marathas held in 1782)

ledger.note: 1739: the Marathas take the Northern Province. 'Most of the Northern Province, including Bassein and Chaul, was lost in 1739 to the Marathas.' Salsette is drawn with it because the Bombay Presidency page has the Marathas cede it to the Company in 1782.
1783: Nagar Haveli. 'The Marathas handed over these territories in 1783'; by 1818 the Portuguese were 'the undisputed rulers of Nagar Haveli'.
1785: 'The Portuguese bought Dadra in 1785.'

region.text: the Novas Conquistas: the Goa talukas taken between 1763 and 1788 from the Dessais of Kudal, the Sondas and the Bhonslas

ledger.counterpart: Dessais of Kudal, Sondas and Bhonslas
ledger.note: 1788: the Novas Conquistas are complete. 'Goa's territory expanded between 1763 and 1788 at the expense of the Dessais of Kudal, the Sondas, and the Bhonslas/Marathas of Silvassa.' The page gives the span, not the years of each taluka.
1843: 'the capital was moved to Panjim' (Nova Goa); the viceroys had lived there since 1 December 1759.

ledger.counterpart: United Front of Goans (Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli)
ledger.note: July 1954: Dadra. 'UFG forces stormed the Dadra police station' on 22 July 1954 (the Portuguese India page gives 24 July for the United Front of Goans taking Dadra).

ledger.counterpart: Azad Gomantak Dal (Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli)
ledger.note: August 1954: Nagar Haveli. 'The Portuguese administrator and police in Nagar Haveli surrendered to Indian police' on 11 August 1954 (the Portuguese India page: seized by the Azad Gomantak Dal on 2 August); 'the Salazar regime lost de facto control' of both enclaves.

17 December 1961: 'Hostilities at Goa began at 09:45 on 17 December 1961' when Indian troops occupied Maulinguem; the main assault began at 04:00 on 18 December; Daman and Diu were attacked on 18 December.

19 December 1961: Daman surrendered at 11:00, Diu at 12:00 and the Governor General Manuel Antonio Vassalo e Silva signed the instrument of surrender for Goa at 20:30. The war lasted two days (22 Indian and 30 Portuguese dead).

region.text: Goa, Daman and Diu, the last three territories

ledger.note: 19 December 1961: Portuguese India ends, 'ending 451 years of Portuguese rule' (Portuguese India page: 'the Governor ... signed the Instrument of Surrender on 19 December 1961'). Goa, Daman and Diu become a union territory under a military governor; a treaty of 31 December 1974 recognised Indian sovereignty.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa

zones.text: Goa: the island of Tiswadi with Old Goa, taken from Bijapur

wars.outcome: Albuquerque captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510 and held it.

wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War (Malabar campaign)

zones.text: Fort Manuel and the Portuguese enclave at Cochin

wars.outcome: Quilon fell 8 December 1661, Cranganore 1662, Cochin 6/7 January 1663, Cannanore 15 February 1663: the Portuguese lost the Malabar forts and moved the garrisons to Goa.

wars.name: Maratha conquest of the Northern Province

zones.text: most of the Northern Province including Bassein and Chaul (and Salsette, which the Marathas held in 1782)

wars.outcome: Bassein and Chaul and most of the Northern Province lost in 1739.
wars.note: The page gives no month or campaign name.

wars.name: Liberation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli
wars.outcome: Dadra taken 22/24 July 1954, Nagar Haveli 2 or 11 August 1954; the Portuguese lost de facto control of both.
wars.note: The two pages give different days.

wars.name: Portuguese wars with the Zamorin of Calicut
wars.outcome: Intermittent war from the Zamorin's 1502 demand that the Portuguese factors leave Kochi to the peace sued for in 1540 by Chinna Kutti Ali; the Zamorin page names the 1526 Siege of Calicut and gives no treaty year.
wars.note: No border change is dated on the page; the Portuguese kept Cochin as a protectorate.

wars.name: Annexation of Goa
wars.outcome: 17-19 December 1961: Indian forces overran Goa, Daman and Diu; the Portuguese surrendered on 19 December.

certainty.note: Forts, islands and ports with no surveyed boundary; the Novas Conquistas of 1763-1788 are known only as a span.
The enclaves and Goa follow administrative talukas; the frontier with British India was fixed by treaty and survey, and Goa, Daman and Diu are the 20th-century lines.

sources.title: Portuguese India
sources.note: Identity (established 15 Aug 1505, ended 19 Dec 1961, area 4,305 km2), capitals, every dated acquisition and loss: Goa 1510, Rachol 1520, the Gujarat gifts 1534-1539, Bassein 1739, the New Conquests 1763-1788, Dadra and Nagar Haveli 1783/1785, 1954, 1961.

sources.title: Annexation of Goa
sources.note: Indian operation of 17-19 December 1961 (Goa, Daman, Diu); Dadra and Nagar Haveli July-August 1954; 31 December 1974 treaty.

sources.title: Dutch Malabar
sources.note: Dutch conquest of the Portuguese Malabar forts: Quilon 8 Dec 1661, Cranganore 1662, Cochin 6/7 Jan 1663, Cannanore 15 Feb 1663.

sources.title: Maldivian Sultanate
sources.note: 1558: a Portuguese garrison on Male; 1573: driven out by Muhammad Thakurufaanu.

sources.title: Zamorin of Calicut
sources.note: 1498 Vasco da Gama at Calicut; 1502 the Zamorin demands the Portuguese factors leave Kochi; the 1526 Siege of Calicut; 1540 peace sued for.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks as a row of its own: Cliopatria draws the Portuguese holdings of India inside 'Portuguese Empire' and 'Portuguese Colonies' (both reviewed by the portuguese-empire dossier of group am-06, which has the Indian events to 1910 and ends in 1910; sa-06-a's notes explain why no portuguese-colonies dossier exists). This dossier adds the State of India as its own state from 1505 to 1961 because the scope names Goa as a dated possession and the 1910-1961 years (the Portuguese Republic and Estado Novo) have no Indian shape of record. cliopatria_names is empty and all keyframes are new. Overlap: the Indian cells drawn by portuguese-empire's keyframes for 1505-1910 should be dropped from that dossier's shapes when this one is drawn (the same advice sa-06-a gives for Ceylon).

Three pages opened (Portuguese India, Annexation of Goa, Dutch Malabar); WebFetch returned extracts. South Asian possessions only: Malacca (1511) and Ormuz (1515) are 'added to the State' on the Portuguese India page but have their own dossiers (portuguese-malacca; Ormuz has none); Macau and Timor are the portuguese-empire's; Mozambique (separated 1752 on the page), Quilon's later settlement and the forts of Cannanore and Cranganore (named only on the Dutch Malabar page) are not drawn.

Page disagreements: Dadra taken on 22 July (Annexation of Goa) or 24 July 1954 (Portuguese India); Nagar Haveli on 11 August (Annexation of Goa) or 2 August 1954 (Portuguese India); Cochin fell on 6 January (body of Dutch Malabar) or 7 January 1663 (its lead); the Dutch Malabar page says the Portuguese had lost Quilon in 1658-59 before the Dutch took it on 8 December 1661; the Portuguese India page says the capital moved from Velha Goa to Panjim in 1843 while the viceroys lived at Panjim from 1759. Page silent: the Portuguese India page does not mention the loss of Cochin in 1663 (Dutch Malabar supplies it), Hughli, Nagapattinam, Mylapore as territory, the Malabar forts of Cannanore and Cranganore, or the 1779 date for Nagar Haveli (1783 on the page).

Area: the infobox 4,305 km2 (no year) equals the Goa, Daman, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli of the 20th century (Goa 3,702, Nagar Haveli 491, Daman 72, Diu 40). The 1954-1961 keyframe (Goa, Daman, Diu) resolves to about 4,050 km2 on the grid with circles; the 1785-1787 keyframe, which holds Dadra and Nagar Haveli, about 4,300 km2. The Annexation of Goa page gives 'around 1,540 square miles (4,000 km2)' for Goa, Daman and Diu.

Gazetteer names absent: Daman (72.85 E 20.41 N), Dadra (73.0, 20.33), Rachol (73.98, 15.29), Bassein/Vasai (72.83, 19.35), Chaul (72.93, 18.55), Salsette (72.98, 19.17), Margao (73.95, 15.28); Goa island is a 25 km disc round 73.92 E 15.5 N.
